result.title: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials
result.summary: Recent work has improved computer-use agents (CUAs) by combining retrieved task-relevant tutorials and look-ahead planning using world models with MLLM judges. However, the contribution of each component -- tutorials, the judge, and the world model -- to overall improvement has not been evaluated in isolation. To fill this gap, we first construct OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial: two datasets for CUAs with curated multimodal tutorials, covering everyday and scientific domains. We then propose RAG-PolicyJudge (RAG-PJ), a policy-judge framework for CUAs conditioned on task-specific tutorials: the policy proposes candidate actions, and the judge selects among them. To isolate the effect of world models given tutorials, we compare RAG-PJ with and without common world models: using either zero-shot text-based descriptions of next states or an oracle that returns ground-truth visual observations. We find that RAG-PJ gains little benefit from these rollouts when tutorials are present, even with perfect visual futures. This suggests prior world-model gains in tutorial-conditioned methods come mainly from tutorial understanding and the judge's ability to select the proposed actions, rather than from predicted rollouts. Error analysis reveals that the bottleneck is not rollout fidelity, but the judge's ability to reason over future states and recognize task completion. This highlights the need to improve not just next-state prediction in world models, but also reasoning over their predicted rollouts. Datasets and code are available at https://github.com/realjoenguyen/RAGPJ-official.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建带多模态教程的 CUA 数据集，提出由 policy 提议动作、judge 选择的 RAG-PolicyJudge 框架，并在有教程条件下对比无世界模型、文本预测下一状态与 oracle 真实视觉未来，发现 rollout 带来的收益很小。
AI.relevance_reason: 该负结果直接拆解了教程、judge 与预测视觉未来的贡献，指出瓶颈在 judge 对未来状态的推理和完成判定，可供核查 LVR 中「预测状态是否被真正使用」、视觉旁路及验证器作用。
